questions.question: Before you start the engine, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have their seat belts on.
Make sure only adult passengers have their seat belts on.
Make sure only child passengers have their seat belts on.
Make sure all passengers have their seat belts on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have their seat belts on.
questions.explanation: Before you start the engine, buckle your own seat belt. Then check that everyone else in the car has buckled theirs too.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, do three things: signal early, check both mirrors, and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder than daytime driving?

options.text: Cars overheat faster at night.
You cannot see as far in the dark.
It rains more at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can only see as far as your headlights reach. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
You can only turn from certain lanes.
Do not enter.
Both lanes must merge safely together.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. It is reserved for buses and cars with the driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp right turn ahead.
A road is joining from the right.
The road will turn sharply right, then sharply left.
The road ahead winds back and forth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will turn sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Get your license and registration ready before the officer gets to your car.
Stay in your car with both hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the police car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with both hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel when stopped. Ask passengers to keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving once you think the children are done getting off.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended. Do not move until the arm is put away.

questions.question: What counts as reasonable help for injured people after a crash?

options.text: Calling for medical help.
Putting pressure on wounds or bandaging them.
Arranging a ride for the injured.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you are in a crash, help injured people if you can. This includes calling for medical help, bandaging wounds, or arranging rides for them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: An intersection is ahead.
A steep downhill section is ahead.
The road ahead winds back and forth.
Traffic is merging ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep downhill section is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill section is coming.

questions.question: In a construction zone, what should you be ready for?

options.text: Having to stop.
Having to change lanes.
Sudden movements from workers or equipment.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In a construction zone, slow down or stop for workers and equipment. Be ready to change lanes. Be ready for sudden movements from workers and equipment.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Give the vehicle extra space.
Know that the driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not copy the driver's behavior.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. Do not look at passengers, search for things in your car, read, or daydream. If another driver seems distracted, stay far back. A distracted driver is more likely to crash.

questions.question: Which substance can make it unsafe to drive and cause a DUII arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and liquor
Illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants like glue or paint
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many substances can affect your driving ability. This includes alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many medicines (both prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is coming toward you with flashing red or blue lights. What should you do?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of the way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles pass. Pull to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on a bridge over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guard rail.

questions.question: One of your tires blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard immediately.
Keep the wheel straight and slow down by easing off the gas pedal.
Keep going at the same speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel straight and slow down by easing off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the wheel firmly and keep the car going straight. Take your foot off the gas pedal slowly. Do not use the brakes until you have control. When safe, brake gently and pull off the road.

questions.question: Is texting while driving allowed?

options.text: Yes, when there are few cars around.
No, never.
Yes, if using voice-to-text.
Yes, if it only takes a few seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to read, write, or send messages on a cell phone while driving. Do not answer calls or texts while driving. Violating this law can result in fines.

questions.question: An aggressive driver cuts you off. What should you do?

options.text: Call the police right away.
Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Do something to get even with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get away from them. Do not try to get even. This can make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar car from a friend. What should you do?

options.text: Do not worry because all cars are the same.
Do not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with it.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take time to learn where the controls are and how they work before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take time to learn where the controls are and how they work before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, spend a few minutes learning where the turn signals, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn are. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to break down the alcohol over time.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol over time.
questions.explanation: Only time will lower your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers can help you stay awake but do not reduce alcohol in your blood or make you sober.

questions.question: What happens if you leave an accident scene where someone was hurt or killed?

options.text: You go to jail only.
You pay a fine only.
You go to jail and pay a fine.
Nothing happens.

questions.correctAnswerText: You go to jail and pay a fine.
questions.explanation: If you are in a crash that injures or kills someone, you must stop right away and stay at the scene. If you left, you must return and stay there immediately.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Exit at the next exit and return to the one you missed.
Roll down your window and ask another driver for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit at the next exit and return to the one you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Instead, go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver cuts you off?

options.text: Pull next to them and yell.
Stay calm and move on.
Flash your high beams at them.
Cut them off to get even.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move on.
questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Stay calm and keep driving safely to avoid road rage.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a vehicle on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and go through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait for it to pass safely before you proceed.

questions.question: What should you do when you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Follow closely behind them.
Show them you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between your vehicle and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car ahead stops suddenly.
You may not see the turn signals.
You may not see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car ahead stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, you won't have enough time to stop safely if the vehicle in front stops suddenly, which can cause a crash.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Drive at normal speed.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give the right-of-way to blind pedestrians with a white cane or guide dog. Be ready to stop to prevent injury or danger.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for the conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What must you do when you hear a fire engine siren behind you?

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull to the curb or side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: When can you leave your car running while you are not in it?

options.text: If you are only leaving for a few minutes.
Never.
If you are idling near a railroad crossing.
If you are idling in an unfamiliar area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to leave your car running and unattended. You must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the brake. The only exception is if you use a remote starter device.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a warning sign?

options.text: Pay close attention to what is ahead.
Follow the sign's instructions.
Reduce your speed if the sign suggests it.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell you about conditions ahead. Pay attention to your surroundings, follow the sign's instructions, and slow down if the sign recommends it.
